faq.q: Is registration of a rent agreement mandatory in Maharashtra?
faq.a: Yes. Section 55 of the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 makes registration compulsory for every leave and licence agreement, whatever its term, and puts the duty on the owner. If it is not registered, the tenant's account of the terms prevails in a dispute, and the owner can be fined up to ₹5,000 or jailed for up to three months.

faq.q: How is stamp duty calculated?
faq.a: For Leave & License (Article 36A), stamp duty is 0.25% of the total of: rent for the full period, including any agreed increases, + any non-refundable deposit + 10% of the refundable deposit for each year of the term. The duty is paid in whole hundreds: it is rounded up to the next ₹100, and is never less than ₹100.

faq.q: What is the registration fee?
faq.a: ₹1,000 for properties in municipal / urban areas and ₹500 for properties in rural (Gram Panchayat) areas.

faq.q: Why is the agreement usually for 11 months?
faq.a: Mostly habit, and a shorter term means less stamp duty and a chance to renegotiate at renewal. In Maharashtra it does not avoid registration: every leave and licence agreement must be registered, whether it runs 11 months or 60. You can choose any term up to 60 months here.

faq.q: Do all parties need to be physically present?
faq.a: No. With e-registration and doorstep biometric (thumb impression), the process can be completed from home for owner, tenant and witnesses.

faq.q: What documents do I need?
faq.a: PAN and Aadhaar of owner and tenant, owner's ownership proof (Index II / electricity bill), passport photos, and two witnesses with ID.

faq.q: Is the instant estimate accurate?
faq.a: It's a free, indicative range from current locality rates and your inputs — great for a quick idea. For an exact, official figure you need a certified valuation with a physical inspection.

faq.q: What is a certified valuation report?
faq.a: A signed report by a qualified valuer detailing the property's fair market value, with the method and comparables used.

faq.q: How is property value calculated?
faq.a: Mainly the comparable-sales method (recent deals nearby) cross-checked with ready-reckoner rates, adjusted for area, age, floor, amenities and condition.

faq.q: How long does it take and what does it cost?
faq.a: The report timeline depends on the property and is confirmed with you before the inspection. Fees are fixed and shared upfront — the instant online estimate is always free.

faq.q: Will banks accept this valuation?

timeline.d: We run a 30-year title search and pull the Encumbrance Certificate to confirm a clear, marketable title.

Buyer, seller and two witnesses sign before the registering officer; photos & biometrics captured on site.
We book your IGR appointment and submit the documents at the Sub-Registrar office for registration.
A unique registration number is allotted; the registered deed is collected and handed to you in 3–7 days.

faq.q: What are the stamp duty and registration charges in Pune?
faq.a: Within PMC and PCMC limits stamp duty is 7% (5% stamp duty + 1% local body tax + 1% metro cess) and the registration fee is 1% of the value, capped at ₹30,000. Charges are calculated on the higher of the agreement value or the government ready-reckoner rate.

faq.q: Is online property registration possible?
faq.a: You can fill details, pay stamp duty & fees and book the appointment online, but physical presence at the Sub-Registrar office for biometrics and signatures is mandatory. We handle the online steps and coordinate the visit.

faq.q: Why is title verification important?
faq.a: A 30-year title search and Encumbrance Certificate confirm the seller's ownership and that the property is free of loans, disputes or charges — protecting you before you pay.

faq.q: How long does registration take?
faq.a: Once documents are ready, execution and registration happen in a single appointment; the registered deed is typically available within 3–7 working days.

faq.q: Does Draazy charge separately for this?
faq.a: Yes — legal services carry a transparent, fixed professional fee (separate from government stamp duty & registration charges), shared with you upfront before you proceed.
